key_errors: ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement openvino~=2027.0.0.dev (from versions: ... 2026.4.1, 2026.5.1.dev20261116)
ERROR: No matching distribution found for openvino~=2027.0.0.dev

root_cause: The tokenizers extension build step installs the just-built local openvino wheel (openvino-2026.5.1.dev20261116), but openvino_tokenizers' pyproject.toml pins its runtime dependency via a floating dev constraint (openvino~=2027.0.0.dev) that tracks the NEXT unreleased minor version rather than the version actually produced by this build. Since no openvino~=2027.0.0.dev package has ever been published to the pip index (the newest available is 2026.5.1.dev20261116), pip's build-dependency resolution for openvino_tokenizers fails outright on Windows, independent of the PR's own change (src/bindings/python/src/pyopenvino/utils/utils.cpp), which is unrelated to tokenizers packaging. This mirrors a long-standing, recurring version-skew issue between the main repo's dev version bump and the openvino_tokenizers submodule/requirement pin.
reproduction_steps: On a Windows build matching the CI image: build the core openvino wheel as done in the workflow (set-up to produce openvino-2026.5.1.dev20261116), then run `python3 -m pip wheel -v --no-deps --wheel-dir build --find-links install/wheels --config-settings override=cmake.build_args=... .` from the openvino_tokenizers checkout. pip will fail resolving `openvino~=2027.0.0.dev` as a build dependency because no such package version is published on PyPI/the internal pip proxy.
recommended_actions: Pin/update the openvino_tokenizers submodule (or its pyproject.toml/setup.cfg openvino dependency constraint) to track the currently published dev series (e.g. ~=2026.5.0.dev or a floating range covering 2026.x) rather than the next unreleased 2027.0.0 series.
Alternatively, have the tokenizers build step pass --no-build-isolation or supply the locally built openvino wheel to satisfy the build-time dependency instead of resolving from the pip index.
Coordinate the openvino_tokenizers version bump with the main repo's dev version bump schedule so this constraint window never points at an unpublished next-major/minor series.
prevention_strategies: Add a CI check (or dependabot-like bot) that validates the openvino_tokenizers submodule's required openvino version range against the currently publishable dev version range before merging a version bump to the main repo. Consider a scheduled smoke job that runs just the tokenizers wheel build against the nightly openvino dev wheel to catch this drift before it blocks the merge queue.
historical_context: This is a recurring pattern (signature_hash 8d60fd1266878935) observed 6 times since 2026-08-27, previously affecting PRs #39236, #37686, #37690, and now #39556. Every occurrence has the identical root cause: the openvino_tokenizers build-time openvino version constraint lags or over-shoots the version actually available on pip.
